The premise that the title only moved to the Petronas Towers in 1998 is incorrect. The Petronas Towers are the tallest in the world, but the title of "tallest outside North America" was held by the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong (completed 1989, height ~367m) from 1989 until 1991, and then by the World Financial Center in New York (which is in North America, so this doesn't count). Actually, the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong surpassed One Raffles Place in 1989. The title of "tallest outside North America" went to the Bank of China Tower in 1989. The Petronas Towers are the tallest in the world, but they are also the tallest outside North America. However, the Bank of China Tower (Hong Kong) was the successor to One Raffles Place as the tallest *outside North America* in 1989. The Planner's logic that the title only moved in 1998 ignores the existence of the Bank of China Tower. The correct successor is the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong. Therefore, the Planner's decision to search for the Petronas Towers is based on false historical data and will lead to an incorrect answer.
